_comment: Firefox enterprise policy. Deploy to whichever of these Firefox reads:
Windows : %ProgramFiles%\Mozilla Firefox\distribution\policies.json
or HKLM\Software\Policies\Mozilla\Firefox (ADMX)
macOS   : /Applications/Firefox.app/Contents/Resources/distribution/policies.json
or the com.mozilla.Firefox configuration profile
Linux   : /etc/firefox/policies/policies.json
THREE THINGS THAT ARE DIFFERENT FROM CHROME AND WILL BITE YOU:
1. HOST PERMISSIONS ARE OPTIONAL IN MV3. Firefox does not auto-grant
host_permissions the way Chrome does. An extension installed normally
sits there with no site access and reports nothing, silently. Two ways
out, both used below: install it force_installed (Firefox 138+ locks
host permissions on for force-installed MV3 extensions, and 153+ stops
the user changing them at all), and set runtime_allowed_hosts.
2. THE EXTENSION ID IS THE GECKO ID, not a 32-char hash. It comes from
browser_specific_settings.gecko.id in the manifest --
dlp-guard@fortbendcountytx.gov -- and it is stable across builds,
which is genuinely easier than Chrome's key-pinning dance.
3. NO chrome.identity.getProfileUserInfo. Attribution MUST come from
workstationTag. If you skip it, every Firefox event lands as
'unattributed' and nobody notices until an incident needs a name.
Unsigned XPIs will not install in release Firefox. Either submit to AMO as
an unlisted add-on (Mozilla signs it, you self-host the XPI) or standardize
on Firefox ESR, which honors the ExtensionSettings install_url for signed
add-ons only. There is no supported way to run an unsigned extension on
release Firefox -- plan for AMO unlisted signing in the project timeline.

_comment_hosts: Firefox 153+ honors runtime_allowed_hosts to grant host permissions
administratively. On earlier versions force_installed + MV3 grants
the declared host_permissions from 138 onward. Below 138 the
extension will install but have no site access -- test this on your
actual ESR version before rollout, because the failure is silent.

_comment_devtools: Consider BlockAboutAddons if your threat model includes an employee
disabling the add-on. It cannot be disabled when force_installed, but
about:debugging can still be used to inspect it. Weigh that against the
help-desk cost of locking down about: pages fleet-wide.
